description: Small, dependency-ordered Ralph work items for the one-bot persistence gate and playable companion MVP. KAP-543 remains the outcome epic; completed Jira stories retain evidence status, while review repairs and integration proofs stay open.

userStories.title: Diagnose the pinned candidate test-configuration mismatch
userStories.description: As the personal server operator, I want diagnose the pinned candidate test-configuration mismatch so the living-world rollout is safe and testable.
acceptanceCriteria:
Scenario: Diagnose the pinned candidate test-configuration mismatch
Given a pinned candidate and a head-provided build status
When the regression extraction marker is compared with its current source
Then the report identifies the missing contract and distinguishes unexecuted tests from failed tests

Scenario: Reject or handle the failure path
Given a proposed repair would change the meaning of the tested behavior
When this condition is detected
Then the worker records that uncertainty rather than deleting the assertion to obtain a pass
userStories.notes: Read-only source comparison; report exact revision and bounded source references. No duplicate server build while the head's probe is running.

userStories.title: Record the smallest viable bot-engine integration boundary
userStories.description: As the personal server operator, I want record the smallest viable bot-engine integration boundary so the living-world rollout is safe and testable.
acceptanceCriteria:
Scenario: Record the smallest viable bot-engine integration boundary
Given the bundled-engine blockers and pinned candidate findings
When the head reviews the proposed execution-engine boundary
Then an ADR lists selected reuse, required host hooks, excluded changes and unresolved runtime proof

Scenario: Reject or handle the failure path
Given a dependency requires unrelated core scheduling or content changes
When this condition is detected
Then it is separated for review rather than silently importing the whole fork
userStories.notes: Worker proposes only; head records the architecture decision. Reopen at most the referenced host interfaces before expanding scope.

userStories.title: Add opt-in world-processing-time measurements
userStories.description: As the personal server operator, I want add opt-in world-processing-time measurements so the living-world rollout is safe and testable.
acceptanceCriteria:
Scenario: Add opt-in world-processing-time measurements
Given a disposable zero-bot world with measurements enabled
When world updates and intentional frame sleeps run
Then bounded telemetry reports processing-time counts and p95/p99 separately from elapsed tick intervals

Scenario: Reject or handle the failure path
Given telemetry is disabled or its output consumer is unavailable
When this condition is detected
Then the world remains nonblocking and retains bounded memory
userStories.notes: Compile server; test known duration samples, percentile edges and disabled mode; run disposable baseline. No live deployment.

userStories.title: Specify persistent bot ownership and save invariants
userStories.description: As the personal server operator, I want specify persistent bot ownership and save invariants so the living-world rollout is safe and testable.
acceptanceCriteria:
Scenario: Specify persistent bot ownership and save invariants
Given persistent and ephemeral bots have different intended lifetimes
When identity, login, save and logout paths are specified
Then the contract binds a persistent bot to a real owned account and character while preserving ephemeral no-save behavior

Scenario: Reject or handle the failure path
Given session account identity disagrees with character ownership
When this condition is detected
Then the contract rejects login/save and never reassigns a human character
userStories.notes: Source-backed design only; head approves before schema or save-path changes. Include interrupted provisioning and stale callback cases.

userStories.title: Add versioned bot-ownership metadata migrations
userStories.description: As the personal server operator, I want add versioned bot-ownership metadata migrations so the living-world rollout is safe and testable.
acceptanceCriteria:
Scenario: Add versioned bot-ownership metadata migrations
Given a disposable character database and an approved identity contract
When the ownership metadata migration is applied and the updater is rerun
Then stable bot identity, ownership, type and provisioning version are retained without duplicate records

Scenario: Reject or handle the failure path
Given a metadata row references an unowned or incompatible character
When this condition is detected
Then validation reports the mismatch without changing human records
userStories.notes: Use the actual updater directory verified in source; migration tests in a disposable database, including an existing-character fixture. No live migration.

userStories.title: Validate persistent bot ownership before session login
userStories.description: As the personal server operator, I want validate persistent bot ownership before session login so the living-world rollout is safe and testable.
acceptanceCriteria:
Scenario: Validate persistent bot ownership before session login
Given a registered persistent bot and matching real account/character ownership
When the bot requests a session
Then login uses the approved account identity and preserves the character's stored owner

Scenario: Reject or handle the failure path
Given ownership is mismatched or a conflicting session exists
When this condition is detected
Then login is rejected without replacing the human session or rewriting ownership
userStories.notes: Compile; isolated valid-owner, wrong-owner and conflicting-session tests. Adapt to the approved engine; do not retain synthetic IDs for persistent saves.

userStories.title: Enable saving only for explicitly owned persistent bots
userStories.description: As the personal server operator, I want enable saving only for explicitly owned persistent bots so the living-world rollout is safe and testable.
acceptanceCriteria:
Scenario: Enable saving only for explicitly owned persistent bots
Given an authenticated bot session satisfies the approved persistent ownership contract
When normal character save executes
Then earned state is written under the existing real owner through normal save paths

Scenario: Reject or handle the failure path
Given the bot is ephemeral or ownership validation fails
When this condition is detected
Then the existing no-save protection remains effective and unrelated human records are unchanged
userStories.notes: Compile; disposable save tests for persistent, ephemeral and mismatched identities. Do not merely remove GetBot() guard.
userStories.acceptanceState: Implemented and Jira Done; review follow-up is represented by MVP-001 or MVP-002.

userStories.title: Repair bundled bot initialization and null-entry safety
userStories.description: As the personal server operator, I want repair bundled bot initialization and null-entry safety so the living-world rollout is safe and testable.
acceptanceCriteria:
Scenario: Repair bundled bot initialization and null-entry safety
Given a newly constructed or detached bundled bot controller
When its first update executes
Then all decision timers have deterministic initialization and a null player is checked before dereference

Scenario: Reject or handle the failure path
Given a valid player is completing a teleport
When this condition is detected
Then required acknowledgement handling remains reachable and correct
userStories.notes: Compile; meaningful null/first-update/teleport fixtures. If the approved engine replaces this class, head records supersession and remaps the test rather than performing an obsolete edit.

userStories.title: Make repeated and stale bot logins lifecycle-safe
userStories.description: As the personal server operator, I want make repeated and stale bot logins lifecycle-safe so the living-world rollout is safe and testable.
acceptanceCriteria:
Scenario: Make repeated and stale bot logins lifecycle-safe
Given one owned bot is loading or online
When the same add request is repeated
Then one session and one matching state transition exist with accurate loading/online counters

Scenario: Reject or handle the failure path
Given an old asynchronous completion arrives after cancellation and retry
When this condition is detected
Then its generation is rejected and the current session is preserved
userStories.notes: Compile; asynchronous login failure, duplicate add, cancellation/retry and logout tests. Online means successful player entry, not merely queued SQL.
userStories.acceptanceState: Implemented and Jira Done; review follow-up is represented by MVP-001 or MVP-002.

userStories.title: Provision one persistent test bot idempotently
userStories.description: As the personal server operator, I want provision one persistent test bot idempotently so the living-world rollout is safe and testable.
acceptanceCriteria:
Scenario: Provision one persistent test bot idempotently
Given an empty disposable lab and one requested bot identity
When provisioning runs twice
Then exactly one valid owned account and character exist with resumable provisioning status

Scenario: Reject or handle the failure path
Given the first run stops between account and character creation
When this condition is detected
Then retry completes the same identity without deleting unrelated records
userStories.notes: Use native account/character creation paths; test at each interruption boundary. One identity only; normal class/race legality and no copied human character data.

userStories.title: Exercise ownership rejection at the save boundary
userStories.description: Exercise ownership rejection at the save boundary
acceptanceCriteria:
Scenario: Reject an invalid persistent save at execution time
Given an owned bot is logged in and its ownership becomes invalid immediately before SaveToDB
When periodic or logout save reaches the ownership guard
Then the save is rejected and character, inventory and quest rows remain unchanged

Scenario: Keep ephemeral sessions unsaved
Given an ephemeral bot session reaches the same save boundary
When SaveToDB executes
Then the existing no-save behavior remains effective
userStories.notes: Accepted from ownership-boundary lab evidence; full card: docs/bots/ralph/mvp/mvp-001.md
userStories.jiraStatus: Mapped locally; Jira parent status unchanged

userStories.title: Deliver and reject a stale login completion
userStories.description: Deliver and reject a stale login completion
acceptanceCriteria:
Scenario: Reject an old generation after retry
Given generation one was cancelled and generation two is current
When a deterministic test hook delivers generation one completion
Then the old completion is rejected and generation two remains authoritative

Scenario: Disable the hook by default
Given a normal server configuration
When bot login runs
Then no synthetic completion can be injected
userStories.notes: Accepted from 7/7 lifecycle and stale-generation lab evidence; full card: docs/bots/ralph/mvp/mvp-002.md
userStories.jiraStatus: Mapped locally; Jira parent status unchanged

userStories.title: Prevent autonomous attacks on players and friendly units
userStories.description: Prevent autonomous attacks on players and friendly units
acceptanceCriteria:
Scenario: Select only legal hostile NPC targets
Given an idle owned bot can see its owner, friendly units, neutral units and a hostile creature
When autonomous target selection runs
Then only a legal hostile creature may be attacked

Scenario: Never initiate PvP autonomously
Given any player is within the scan radius
When the bot is not already defending itself
Then it does not initiate an attack on that player
userStories.notes: Accepted: source/build guard plus 2/2 disposable two-faction target-policy lifecycle lab; full card: docs/bots/ralph/mvp/mvp-003.md
userStories.jiraStatus: Mapped locally; Jira parent status unchanged

userStories.title: Prove legitimate combat XP for one owned bot
userStories.description: Prove legitimate combat XP for one owned bot
acceptanceCriteria:
Scenario: Earn XP through normal combat credit
Given one owned bot and a deterministic eligible hostile creature in a disposable world
When the bot kills the creature through normal combat
Then its XP increases through the server credit path and the before/after evidence names the bot identity
userStories.notes: Accepted: normal combat against Kobold Vermin changed owned bot XP from 0 to 54; full card: docs/bots/ralph/mvp/mvp-004.md
userStories.jiraStatus: Mapped locally; Jira parent status unchanged

userStories.title: Add one bounded normal corpse-loot interaction
userStories.description: Add one bounded normal corpse-loot interaction
acceptanceCriteria:
Scenario: Loot one eligible corpse through game handlers
Given the owned bot killed a creature with deterministic loot
When its bounded loot action executes
Then the item enters inventory through normal loot rules and no item is fabricated by SQL or GM command

Scenario: Respect ownership and capacity
Given loot is unavailable, reserved, or inventory is full
When the bot tries to loot
Then it does not duplicate or take the item illegally
userStories.notes: Accepted 2026-09-13: held-target combat + normal corpse loot proved in a disposable lab (python docker/test_bot_loot.py -v, 1/1 in 62.2s). Bot Lootbot GUID:500102 killed seeded Kobold Vermin 2500002 via normal combat and looted item 117 through SendLoot/Unit::Kill paths: 'corpse loot stored GUID:500102 item:117 before:0 after:1'. Root cause of the earlier 0-slot loot: fresh lab DBs replayed all 149 sql/database_updates files at world start (base dump ships an empty legacy migrations table), clobbering the seeded creature_template.loot_id; fixed by docker/init-db-updates.sh applying+recording updates (SHA-1, uppercase) at db init. Full card: docs/bots/ralph/mvp/mvp-005.md
userStories.jiraStatus: Mapped locally; Jira parent status unchanged

userStories.title: Add one declared supported quest progression path
userStories.description: Add one declared supported quest progression path
acceptanceCriteria:
Scenario: Progress one named quest through normal rules
Given one declared low-level quest and an eligible owned bot
When the bot accepts it and performs its supported objective
Then normal quest APIs record progress and the evidence identifies the exact quest and objective

Scenario: Fail closed outside the declared quest
Given a quest is unsupported or prerequisites fail
When progression is requested
Then the bot does not fabricate credit or rewards
userStories.notes: Accepted 2026-09-13 (park-head local-Qwen): declared quest 456 proven end-to-end in two disposable labs (python docker/test_bot_quest.py -v, 7/7 in 305s). Flow lab (Questbot GUID:500104): accepted from seeded NPC 2079, killed 7x2031 + 4x1984 via normal combat, core auto-completed on final credit, bot turned in and was rewarded: 'quest rewarded GUID:500104 quest:456 xpBefore:648 xpAfter:818'; DB row persisted with rewarded=1 and XP saved (0 -> 818); no [CRASH]. Fail-closed lab (no giver): init only, no credit/reward, quest=none xp=0 over 90s; no [CRASH]. Fixes in PlayerBotAI: player chase is a no-op without the chased unit as victim (ChaseMovementGenerator::_lostTarget), so quest-giver pursuit now uses a pathfinding MovePoint; phase 2->3 also transitions on GetQuestStatus==COMPLETE because the core auto-completes and CanCompleteQuest then returns false. Test schema correction: no characters.questlog in this fork; character_queststatus.status uses the fork enum (COMPLETE=1, INCOMPLETE=3) written verbatim, rewarded rows persist with rewarded=1. Debug-gated quest state/req/attack/giver-loss lines added; head-approved one-line GetSpecialFlags() getter in QuestDef.h (observability only). Evidence under gitignored local/. Full card: docs/bots/ralph/mvp/mvp-006.md
userStories.jiraStatus: Mapped locally; Jira parent status unchanged

userStories.title: Prove exact earned state across world restart
userStories.description: Prove exact earned state across world restart
acceptanceCriteria:
Scenario: Preserve earned state after restart
Given recorded identity, XP, legitimate loot and supported quest progress
When the disposable world performs a clean save, stops and restarts
Then the same identity and complete recorded state match after login
userStories.notes: Small MVP work item. Full card: docs/bots/ralph/mvp/mvp-007.md
userStories.jiraStatus: Mapped locally; Jira parent status unchanged

userStories.title: Prove exact earned state after isolated backup restore
userStories.description: Prove exact earned state after isolated backup restore
acceptanceCriteria:
Scenario: Restore earned state into a second disposable project
Given the restart proof passed and a bounded backup exists
When that backup is restored into a separate port-free project
Then identity, ownership, XP, inventory and supported quest state match the source snapshot

Scenario: Protect the personal volume
Given source or target identity is not the expected disposable project
When restore or cleanup is requested
Then the operation stops before changing any volume
userStories.notes: Small MVP work item. Full card: docs/bots/ralph/mvp/mvp-008.md
userStories.jiraStatus: Mapped locally; Jira parent status unchanged

userStories.title: Prove one bot's earned state survives restart and restore
userStories.description: As the personal server operator, I want prove one bot's earned state survives restart and restore so the living-world rollout is safe and testable.
acceptanceCriteria:
Scenario: Prove one bot's earned state survives restart and restore
Given one lab bot has legitimately earned XP, an item and a supported quest update
When the world restarts and a backup is restored into a second disposable project
Then the same bot identity, owner and earned records match the pre-restart evidence

Scenario: Reject or handle the failure path
Given the save or backup is incomplete
When this condition is detected
Then the check fails with bounded evidence and cannot overwrite the personal volume
userStories.notes: Real game/save integration required; compare complete relevant state, not only table existence. Do not use fabricated SQL rewards as gameplay proof.

userStories.title: Add deterministic follow and stop for one owned companion
userStories.description: As the personal server operator, I want add deterministic follow and stop for one owned companion so the living-world rollout is safe and testable.
acceptanceCriteria:
Scenario: Add deterministic follow and stop for one owned companion
Given one owned companion in the human's test party and no LLM service
When the owner issues follow and then stop
Then normal pathfinding follows the leader and stop invalidates the current goal immediately

Scenario: Reject or handle the failure path
Given a different player commands the bot or an old goal is delivered after stop
When this condition is detected
Then the command is rejected and the bot does not resume the invalidated goal
userStories.notes: Compile and isolated command/ownership tests; local in-game follow, range, stop and relog checks. No combat-role or natural-language scope in this story.

userStories.title: Make bot population boundaries deterministic
userStories.description: As the personal server operator, I want make bot population boundaries deterministic so the living-world rollout is safe and testable.
acceptanceCriteria:
Scenario: Make bot population boundaries deterministic
Given roster sizes of zero, one and ten with explicit min/max targets
When the director reconciles requested population
Then exact target boundaries are respected and loading, online and offline counts remain distinct

Scenario: Reject or handle the failure path
Given the requested target exceeds valid roster capacity or a login fails
When this condition is detected
Then actual capacity is reported without underflow, a fake online count or an unbounded retry
userStories.notes: Compile; empty/single/full roster, min=max and failure-boundary tests. Preserve a separate random-range mode only if explicitly required.

userStories.title: Validate a paced ten-bot disposable cohort
userStories.description: As the personal server operator, I want validate a paced ten-bot disposable cohort so the living-world rollout is safe and testable.
acceptanceCriteria:
Scenario: Validate a paced ten-bot disposable cohort
Given ten valid persistent bot identities in a disposable project
When a bounded login schedule activates the cohort
Then ten distinct successful sessions are observed with saved ownership intact and recorded resource/tick measurements

Scenario: Reject or handle the failure path
Given a bot cannot load or resource thresholds are exceeded
When this condition is detected
Then new logins back off and the report identifies the achieved count without repeatedly recreating identities
userStories.notes: Run a 30-minute ten-bot observation after prior gates; no 50+ load or live rollout. Record actual actions separately from online status.

userStories.title: Configure legal persistent-bot race, class, gender and appearance
userStories.description: Allow an operator to declare each persistent bot identity without hardcoded Human Warrior creation.
acceptanceCriteria:
Scenario: Create a configured legal identity
Given a name and legal race, class, gender and appearance specification
When native provisioning runs
Then Player::Create receives that specification and homebind derives from the matching playercreateinfo row

Scenario: Reject an illegal or changed identity
Given an illegal combination or a specification that conflicts with an existing marker
When provisioning runs
Then it fails closed without replacing or mutating the existing character
userStories.notes: Post-MVP. Keep the first playable demo as one Human Warrior. Full card: docs/bots/ralph/mvp/next-001.md
validation: focused provisioning matrix in a disposable project

mvpDefinition.foundationGate: One owned bot earns XP, loot, and supported quest progress through normal game paths; the exact state survives restart and isolated restore.
mvpDefinition.playableCompanion: The foundation gate plus owner-safe targeting and deterministic owner-only follow/stop with no LLM dependency.

selectionPolicy: Choose the lowest-priority-number story with passes=false whose dependencies all pass. Execute one story per fresh session.
